title: Functions, Parameters, and Return Values
summary: Name reusable work, pass values through parameters, and return results to the caller.

sketchBlocks.title: A function gives a repeatable action a name
Parameters let one function work with different values
return lets other code use a function's result

quizDraft.title: Return or display?
quizDraft.prompt: Which statement best describes `return` inside a function?
quizDraft.hint: Think about what the caller can receive from the function.

help.concept: A function can produce a value that later code stores or combines.
help.hint_1: Displaying a value and returning a value are separate responsibilities.
help.hint_2: Choose the option that lets the caller use the result.

options: It always prints the value in the Console.
It sends a result back to the caller.

quizDraft.title: Reason about functions
quizDraft.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
quizDraft.hint: Focus on reuse, inputs, and results.

help.concept: Functions can receive inputs and produce results without necessarily printing.
help.hint_1: A function definition can support many calls with different arguments.
help.hint_2: Reject the statement that makes Console output mandatory.

options: A parameter is a local name for an input.
A function can be called more than once.
`return` can produce a value for the caller.

quizDraft.title: Complete the function result
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the keyword that sends the calculated value back to the caller.
quizDraft.hint: Think about how a caller receives a value produced inside a function.

help.concept: The missing keyword finishes the function with a result.
help.hint_1: It is not a declaration, condition, or array operation.
help.hint_2: Choose the function-control keyword that hands a value back.

quizDraft.title: Trace a function call
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange what happens when a function with one parameter is called.
quizDraft.hint: Separate defining the reusable operation from running one call.

help.concept: A call supplies an argument before the body can use its parameter.
help.hint_1: The body works with the received value.
help.hint_2: A returned result is available only after the function body reaches return.

tokens: Define the function and its parameter
Call the function with an argument
The parameter receives that argument value
The returned value goes back to the caller
correctOrder: Define the function and its parameter
Call the function with an argument
The parameter receives that argument value
The returned value goes back to the caller

quizDraft.title: Create a reusable status message
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: The same ready message is needed in more than one place, and duplicating the same `console.log` line makes future changes harder. Task: Define `showReady()` so it logs `"Ready"`, then call the function twice. Expected result: the Console shows `Ready` twice using one reusable function.
quizDraft.hint: Define the function once; reuse it with two calls.

help.concept: A function definition can be called repeatedly without duplicating its body.
help.hint_1: Put the log statement inside the function body.
help.hint_2: After the closing brace, write two separate `showReady();` calls.

quizDraft.title: Greet different learners
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A greeting feature must work for different learners without creating a separate function for each name. Task: Define `greetLearner(name)` so it logs a template-literal greeting. Call it once with `"Maya"` and once with `"Leo"`. Expected result: the Console shows a personalized greeting for each learner.
quizDraft.hint: One parameter should make the same function work for both names.

help.concept: Parameters let a reusable function receive different input values on different calls.
help.hint_2: Use `${name}` inside a template literal, then make the two calls after the function definition.

quizDraft.title: Calculate an order total
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: An order screen needs the same price-times-quantity calculation for many possible orders, so the calculation should be reusable. Task: Define `calculateTotal(price, quantity)` so it returns their product. Store the result of `calculateTotal(8, 3)` in `total`, then log `total`. Expected result: the Console shows `24`.
quizDraft.hint: The function should produce a value rather than print from inside the function.

help.concept: return sends a calculated value back to the caller.
help.hint_1: Multiply the two parameters inside the function.
help.hint_2: Return the product, store the function call in `total`, and log `total` afterward.
